fp32_vector.flop_convention: tensor_scalar(op0=multiply, op1=add) or activation(identity, scale, bias): one fused a*x+b per element = 2 FLOP; one or two operators cost the same (S8, S9)
fp32_vector.arithmetic_precision: VectorE/ScalarE/GpSimd tensor_scalar arithmetic is always FP32 internally (S3, S8, S9); BF16/FP16 change only the datapath width (VectorE performance mode), not the math. There is no packed half2 FMA comparable to GPU fp16x2/bf16x2.

quotes: Vector Engines are highly parallelized, and deliver a total of 1 TFLOPS of FP32 computations.
Scalar Engines are highly parallelized, and deliver a total of 1.2 TFLOPS of FP32 computations.
documented_engine_tflops_not_used.why_not_used: They equal ~1024 FLOP per engine cycle (1.0e12/0.96e9 = 1042, 1.2e12/1.2e9 = 1000); NeuronCore-v2 figures equal ~2048 FLOP/cycle (2.3e12/1.12e9, 2.9e12/1.4e9, S10/S7) although v3 doubled the VectorE datapath. The counting convention is undocumented and cannot be reproduced from the documented datapath widths with 1 FMA = 2 FLOP (ScalarE would need 7.8 FLOP per lane-cycle). Not an elementwise-FMA bound.

fp32_vector.status_reason: TileArena's vector modes count elementwise FLOPs a kernel may spread over VectorE, ScalarE and GpSimd (the empirical calibration measured all three together). A strict bound for that combined execution needs the GpSimd FMA issue rate (undocumented, S7: 'no rule-of-thumb') and the VectorE/GpSimd shared-bus arbitration (S3), so it is not established. Per-engine bounds below.

VectorE.formula: 2 physical cores x elements/cycle x 2 FLOP x f
VectorE.status_reason: S3 Table 10: '256 input/output for other data types' at 0.96 GHz. Assumption: the 256-element width applies to a single-input tensor_scalar on fp32 data. If the 256 counts both inputs of tensor_tensor (NC-v2 cost model: one-input instruction = N cycles, S7), the fp32 tensor_scalar bound is half (alternative below). The larger value is kept as the upper bound.

ScalarE.formula: 2 physical cores x elements/cycle x 2 FLOP x f
ScalarE.status_reason: S3 Table 10: 128 input/output elements/cycle at 1.2 GHz; activation/tensor_scalar perform a*x+b in one pass at no extra cost (S8, S9). Assumption: one element per lane per cycle in steady state (no ScalarE cost model published for NC-v3).

GpSimd.formula: 2 physical cores x elements/cycle x 2 FLOP x f
GpSimd.status_reason: 8 processors x 512-bit = 128 fp32 lanes at 1.2 GHz (S2, S3, S7); whether a lane retires one fused multiply-add per cycle is undocumented (S7: no cost rule). Value = upper candidate assuming one FMA/lane/cycle; tensor_scalar on GpSimd computes in fp32 (S8), so 16-bit data does not widen it.

assumptions: no SBUF port contention among the three engines (S3 allows VectorE/GpSimd parallel SBUF access)
valid only for kernels that leave GpSimd idle; not a strict bound for the declared mode

hbm_bandwidth.scope: per_logical_neuroncore_lnc2 (2 physical NeuronCore-v3); one HBM stack (24 GB bank)
hbm_bandwidth.traffic_convention: bytes read from HBM + bytes written to HBM (same as TileArena Q, the empirical hbm_stream_bw probes, and Neuron Explorer MBU, T2); the vendor figure is the stack's total (read+write) interface bandwidth, so nothing is doubled for copies
hbm_bandwidth.status_reason: One logical core at LNC=2 owns one of the four HBM banks (S4: each 24 GB bank shared by the two physical cores that form the logical core). AWS's profiler defines hbm_max_bandwidth as 'the maximum HBM bandwidth of a HBM stack ... For LNC1 and LNC2 the same' (T2) and embeds 716.0 GB/s for these exact executions (T1). 4 x 716 = 2.864 TB/s, which the documentation rounds to 2.9 TB/s (S1; S6 46.4/16) and 3 TB/s (S3).
assumptions: A1 TileBench tensors of the logical core reside in its own bank (runtime allocation; not observed directly). DMA engines can address any HBM on the device (S3/S7), so a kernel with data spread over several banks could exceed one stack (then bounded by DMA, below).
A2 The profiler constant is the hardware peak per stack (it is the denominator AWS uses for MBU), not a derated value.
A3 The four stacks are identical (S3: 4 stacks; no unequal split documented; T2 uses a single per-stack value).

A4 Decimal units (1 TB/s = 1e12 B/s): AWS writes 'TB/sec' (S1) but the Trn1 page writes '820 GiB/sec' (S11) where the NKI guide writes '820 GB/s' (S7), so AWS unit spelling is not reliable; the profiler constant 716.0e9 is decimal.

candidates.why_not_selected: 2.9 TB/s is a 2-significant-digit rounding (2.864 -> 2.9, the same rounding maps 4x716 and 8x435 GB/s to the documented 2.9 and 3.5 TB/s); 725 overstates the stack by 1.26 %. Use it instead only if the owner prefers 'never below any documented figure'.
whole device (4 stacks); not accessible to one logical core's local allocation

dma_is_not_hbm.source: T1 (dma_ddr_bandwidth 435.0 GB/s, num_dma_engines_per_neuroncore 16); S1 3.5 TB/s = 8 x 435 rounded; S3 128 engines = 8 x 16; per engine 27.2 GB/s (S7 NC-v2: 27 GiB/s)
dma_is_not_hbm.binding_resource: logical core (2 physical): min(HBM stack 716, DMA 870 [+ GpSimd DMA]) = HBM stack -> HBM-bound. Single physical core (LNC=1 or one core idle): min(716, 435) = DMA-bound at 435 GB/s.
dma_is_not_hbm.not_used_as_roofline: 3.5 TB/s and 870 GB/s are DMA engine throughput, not HBM bandwidth

status_legend.verified: published by AWS for this engine/mode and reproduced from documented array/datapath x clock
status_legend.derived_with_assumptions: computed from documented constants plus explicitly listed assumptions
status_legend.unresolved: no strict bound can be established from available evidence; value null
status_legend.unsupported: hardware/ISA does not support the mode on NeuronCore-v3; value null

analysis: H1 'chip figures use a higher TensorE clock': rejected. The clock that would reproduce each chip figure differs per precision (2.544 / 2.478 / 2.762 / 2.444 GHz); a single physical clock cannot. AWS documents one TensorE frequency (2.4 GHz, S3) and the profiler reports 2.4 GHz for these runs (T1).

H2 'chip figures add non-TensorE engines': consistent but undocumented. chip - 8 x published-per-core is exactly 35 TFLOP/s for FP8, BF16/FP16/TF32 and sparse, and 21 TFLOP/s for FP32 - a precision-independent additive term, as expected if VectorE/ScalarE/GpSimd contributions were added. Its composition cannot be reproduced from the documented per-engine figures (8 x (1.0+1.2) = 17.6 TFLOP/s FP32).
H3 'different power/clock regime for single-core vs full-chip': no documentation found; throttling (T2) only lowers utilization.

Conclusion: per-logical-core TensorE bounds use 2 x the documented per-core derivation (157.29 TFLOP/s BF16/FP16/TF32, 314.57 FP8, 39.32 FP32). Chip/4 (166.75 / 324.75 / 45.25) is recorded but not used; it exceeds the TensorE bound by 6.0 / 3.2 / 15.1 % and, under H2, counts engines that the matrix modes do not represent. A strict bound for a kernel that adds VectorE/ScalarE FLOPs to TensorE FLOPs is unresolved (no TileArena mode mixes them).

per_physical_core_reference.note: a single physical core reaches one HBM stack only through its 16 DMA engines, so its memory ceiling is DMA (435 GB/s), not 716 GB/s

empirical_vs_theoretical_explanations: Throttling: Neuron Explorer reports hardware utilization limited below 100% in 16 of 71 profiled cases (activity and GPIO throttling, T2). matmul fp16 K20480 averaged a 97.1 % utilization limit (non-transpose TensorE rate 140.1 TFLOP/s = 0.891 of 157.29, tool mfu_inst); streamk 86-87 %, batched_matmul 69-71 %, linear_self_attention fp32 11 %. The theoretical bound assumes no throttling.
Clock: no evidence of a clock above or below 2.4 GHz; throttling acts on utilization (T2).

TensorE utilization: each MultiplyMoving has an initiation interval of max(N, 64) cycles with N <= 512 (S7, S5), plus LoadStationary, PSUM evacuation by VectorE/ScalarE and DMA feed; eager torch.matmul schedules come from neuronx-cc, not NKI.
Compiler / precision path: TF32 was reached only through neuronx-cc --auto-cast matmult tf32 (77.2 % of 157.29); the native NKI tfloat32 path was not measured. FP32 IEEE GEMM 36.9 = 93.9 % of 39.32.

Workload size: empirical fp16/bf16/tf32 GEMM throughput falls at the largest sizes (e.g. fp16 118.7 at M=16384), consistent with schedule/throttling effects; the theoretical bound is size-independent.

DMA: HBM copy reaches 672.3 GB/s = 93.9 % of the 716 GB/s stack using 32 DMA engines (870 GB/s capacity). With one physical core, the copy reached 426.5 GB/s = 98 % of that core's 435 GB/s DMA ceiling (calibration diagnostic), i.e. the single-core limit is DMA, the two-core limit is the stack.

Non-matrix engines: measured single-engine FMA chains reach 43 % (VectorE fp32 vs 256-wide bound; 86 % of the 128-wide alternative), 58 % (ScalarE), 54 % (GpSimd candidate); bf16 VectorE 27 % of the 4x-mode bound - the calibration probe (2 dependent chains, free size 2048) did not demonstrate the performance mode.

empirical_calibration_reference.use: consistency checks only; no theoretical value depends on it

sources.title: Neuron Explorer 2.32 metric terminology (exported from the tool)

quotes.S1_compute: Eight NeuronCore-v3 that collectively deliver: 1,299 FP8 TFLOPS; 667 BF16/FP16/TF32 TFLOPS; 2,563 FP8/FP16/BF16/TF32 sparse TFLOPS; 181 FP32 TFLOPS
quotes.S1_mem: 96 GiB of device memory with 2.9 TB/sec of bandwidth.
quotes.S1_dma: 3.5 TB/sec of DMA bandwidth, with inline memory compression and decompression.
quotes.S2_te: A NeuronCore-v3 Tensor Engine delivers 158 cFP8 TFLOPS, and 79 BF16/FP16/TF32 TFLOPS of tensor computations.
quotes.S2_inputs: Tensor Engines support mixed-precision computations, including cFP8, FP16, BF16, TF32, and FP32 inputs and outputs.
quotes.S2_sparse: The NeuronCore-v3 Tensor Engine also supports Structured Sparsity, delivering up to 316 TFLOPS of cFP8/FP16/BF16/TF32 compute.
quotes.S2_vec: Vector Engines are highly parallelized, and deliver a total of 1 TFLOPS of FP32 computations.
quotes.S2_sca: Scalar Engines are highly parallelized, and deliver a total of 1.2 TFLOPS of FP32 computations.
quotes.S2_gps: Each GPSIMD engine consists of eight fully-programmable 512-bit wide vector processors.
quotes.S3_hbm: 4 HBM stacks with a total device memory capacity of 96GiB and bandwidth of 3TB/s.
quotes.S3_dma: 128 DMA (Direct Memory Access) engines to move data within and across devices.
quotes.S3_table: Table 10 Compute Engine Specifications (Trainium2): Tensor 4x128 (dense FP8_E4/FP8_E5 input), 2x128 (dense BF16/FP16 input) or 5x128 (sparse input); 1x128 (output), 2.4 GHz; Vector 512 BF16/FP16 input/output; 256 input/output for other data types, 0.96 GHz; Scalar 128 input/output, 1.2 GHz; GpSimd 1.2 GHz
quotes.S3_te: A NeuronCore-v3 Tensor Engine delivers 158 FP8, 79 BF16/FP16/TF32 and 20 FP32 dense TFLOPS of tensor computations. It also delivers 316 FP8/BF16/FP16/TF32 sparse TFLOPS.
quotes.S3_fp8: each processing element performs two pairs of FP8 multiplications and also accumulation of the two multiplication results per cycle
quotes.S3_fp8e3: FP8_E3 format is still supported by NeuronCore-v3 TensorE similar to NeuronCore-v2, but its matmul performance is the same as BF16/FP16.
quotes.S3_vecperf: NeuronCore-v3 Vector Engine provides a new performance mode BF16/FP16 data types, which quadruples or doubles the instruction throughput depending on the instruction type compared to NeuronCore-v2 ... Enabling this performance mode does not change the computation precision - all computation is still done in FP32
quotes.S3_vec4x: nisa.tensor_copy and nisa.tensor_scalar when both input/output tensors: are in SBUF; are in BF16/FP16 (input and output data types do not need to match); have physically contiguous elements in the inner-most (most minor) free dimension
quotes.S3_bus: VectorE's performance mode leverages a shared memory bus between the VectorE and GpsimdE engines to deliver 2-4x performance improvement for select VectorE instructions. The hardware automatically coordinates access between engines to optimize bus utilization, including arbitrating between GpsimdE and relevant VectorE instructions.
quotes.S3_par: VectorE and GpSimdE can access SBUF in parallel. ... VectorE and ScalarE can access PSUM in parallel.
quotes.S3_16dma: In Trainium2, each NeuronCore-v3 is typically paired with 16x DMA engines to drive its corresponding SBUF bandwidth.
quotes.S3_gpsdma: All eight processors together have a total integrated DMA bandwidth of 307 GB/s (153 GB/s per read/write direction).
quotes.S3_sbuf: NeuronCore-v3 SBUF capacity is 28MiB (or, 128 partitions of 224KiB), up from 24 MiB in NeuronCore-v2.
quotes.S4_lnc: On Trn2, each chip has 8 physical NeuronCores. With LNC=2 (default), these are grouped into 4 Logical NeuronCores.
quotes.S4_bank: Trainium2 devices contain four 24GB HBM banks. Each bank is shared by two physical NeuronCore-v3. When LNC=2, the two physical NeuronCores share a single address space.
quotes.S5_dtypes: The input stationary and moving tiles can be one of these supported data types: float8_e4m3/float8_e5m2/bfloat16/float16/tfloat32/float32. Starting NeuronCore-v4, float8_e4m3fn (OCP FP8) is also supported; float8_e4m3 (legacy) and float8_e4m3fn cannot be mixed in the same matmul.
quotes.S5_array: NeuronCore Tensor Engine is built upon a systolic array with 128 rows and 128 columns of processing elements (PEs).
quotes.S5_acc: The accumulation precision internal to Tensor Engine is float32. The dst tile must be a float32 tile in NeuronCore-v2 and NeuronCore-v3.
quotes.S5_double: matmul_perf_mode.double_row enables double FP8 mode which achieves 2x matmul throughput by packing two FP8 weight/ifmap element pairs and computing two multiplications in parallel per cycle
quotes.S5_onezero: is_stationary_onezero ... setting this field explicitly could lead to 2x better performance if stationary tile is in float32
quotes.S6_inst: trn2.48xlarge: 16 Trainium2 chips; FP8 20.8 PFLOPS; FP16/BF16/TF32 10.7 PFLOPS; Sparse 41 PFLOPS; FP32 2.9 PFLOPS; Device Memory Bandwidth 46.4 TB/sec
quotes.S7_table: Trainium/Inferentia2 (NeuronCore-v2): Tensor 2x128 (input); 1x128 (output), 2.8 GHz; Vector 128 input/output, 1.12 GHz; Scalar 1.4 GHz; GpSimd 1.4 GHz
quotes.S7_te: TensorE supports BF16, FP16, TF32, and cFP8 input matrix data types at a maximum throughput of 92 TFLOPS, as well as 23 TFLOPS for FP32 inputs.
quotes.S7_fp32cost: For FP32 input data type, the instruction cost is roughly 4x higher than BF16/FP16/TF32/cFP8.
quotes.S7_mmcost: The initiation interval between subsequent MM instructions in this case is roughly max(N, MM_INIT_LATENCY), where MM_INIT_LATENCY is 64 TensorE cycles on NeuronCore-v2
quotes.S7_veccost: If there is only one input tile, most VectorE instructions can execute in roughly N cycles (example: nki.isa.tensor_scalar). If there are two input tiles, the instruction can execute in roughly 2N cycles (example: nki.isa.tensor_tensor)
quotes.S7_gps: GpSimdE has 128 parallel compute lanes for 32-bit computation data types across SIMD lanes of all eight processors ... Unlike VectorE/ScalarE, there is no rule-of-thumb to estimate execution cost of a GpSimdE instruction.
quotes.S7_dma: Each DMA engine can process one DMA transfer at a time driving a peak bandwidth of 27 GiB/s
quotes.S8_ts: Apply up to two math operators ... (data <op0> operand0) <op1> operand1 ... performing one operator has the same performance cost as performing two operators in the instruction. ... The Scalar Engine on trn2 only supports some operator combinations: op0=nl.multiply and op1=nl.add ... The compute engine automatically casts data.dtype to float32 and performs the operators in float32 math.
quotes.S9_act: output = op(data * scale + bias) ... All these optional operations incur no further performance penalty compared to only applying the activation function ... The Scalar Engine always performs the math operations in float32 precision.
quotes.S10_v2: The ScalarEngine ... delivers 2.9 TFLOPS of FP32 computations ... The VectorEngine ... delivers 2.3 TFLOPS of FP32 computations ... (cFP8 / FP16 / BF16 / TF32 / FP32 / INT8 inputs, FP32 / INT32 outputs). Each NeuronCore-v2 TensorEngine delivers over 90 TFLOPS of FP16/BF16 tensor computations
quotes.S11_trn1: Two NeuronCore-v2 delivering 380 INT8 TOPS, 190 FP16/BF16/cFP8/TF32 TFLOPS, and 47.5 FP32 TFLOP. 32 GiB of device memory (for storing model state), with 820 GiB/sec of bandwidth.
quotes.T1_meta: num_physical_cores=2, vnc_enabled=true, neuroncore_idx=2, neuron_device_idx=0, instance_type=trn2.3xlarge, tensor_engine_num_rows=128, tensor_engine_num_cols=128, tensor_engine_clock_freq=2.4, vector_engine_clock_freq=0.96, scalar_engine_clock_freq=1.2, gpsimd_engine_clock_freq=1.2, neuroncore_clock_freq=1.2, hbm_ddr_bandwidth=716000002048.0, dma_ddr_bandwidth=434999984128.0, num_dma_engines_per_neuroncore=16
quotes.T2_mbu: Calculated as: (hbm_write_bytes + hbm_read_bytes) / total_time / hbm_max_bandwidth. The hbm_max_bandwidth is the maximum HBM bandwidth of a HBM stack. For LNC1 and LNC2, the hbm_max_bandwidth is the same.
quotes.T2_mfu: each floating point multiply-add is counted as two FLOPs, and tensor_engine_max_ops_per_sec is 2 times the number of Tensor Engine elements times the clock speed.
quotes.T2_throttle: throttle_active_nc0_time_ns: Total time in nsec when hardware utilization was limited to less than 100% due to throttling.
quotes.T2_baseclk: The NeuronCore base clock rate for Inferentia1 is 1.0 GHz, Trainium1 is 1.4 GHz, and Trainium2 is 1.2 GHz.
